title: Dieter Rams, RZ 62 armchair, 1962
lede: Dieter Rams’s lounge chair for Vitsœ: a dark glass-fibre shell of flat side panels, filled with loose upholstered cushions.
summary: Flat dark shell panels with visible fixing bolts, soft square cushions, and a set-back plinth. Rams for Vitsœ, about 1962.

evidence.note: Inspected the V&A’s image 2014HC8620 of object CIRC.430:1-1970 at 1600 × 1540 px, through the V&A IIIF service. The image is a black-and-white photograph, so it does not show color.

styles.note: Rams’s furniture follows his Braun method: flat panels, visible fixings, a modular frame, and no ornament.

context: The V&A dates the chair about 1962 and gives a black matt glass-fibre base, sides, and back, with suede-covered rubberised hair upholstery and a separate seat cushion. The record says it was manufactured by Vitsœ, Eschborn, and relaunched by Vitsœ in 2006. [V&A CIRC.430:1-1970](https://collections.vam.ac.uk/item/O314704/).
The same record quotes R. Hollis (1970): Rams was head of the Product Design Division at Braun AG from 1955. [V&A](https://collections.vam.ac.uk/item/O314704/).
observed: Each side is one flat, dark panel with rounded corners. The armrest is a padded top edge that folds out over the panel.
Two small round bolt heads show on each side panel.
The seat and back are loose, square cushions with soft edges, set inside the shell.
The chair stands on a recessed plinth, so the body appears to float a little above the floor.
interpretation: The chair is the furniture branch of the style: a box of flat parts that is honest about its fixings. It is dark and upholstered, so it fits the structure and surface rules more than the white-and-grey palette.
borrow: Show the fixings as small, regular round details instead of hiding them.
